findings: **Isolated changes:** constrained actions passed 2/10, targeted repair 1/10, alignment 0/10, requirement checks 0/10 and file-version repetition 0/10. None of these single changes beat the frozen baseline. Each was scored on the same task order, suite hash, model digest and budgets.

**Structured decoding repaired the protocol bottleneck.** The [constrained run](runs/20261106T205236Z-v0-constrained-qwen3-5-4b-q4-K-M-mini10-f918c1/tasks.jsonl) had 1 parse error and 0 format-budget exits. Its sole malformed action was a response cut off at the unchanged token limit, recorded in [toposort](runs/20261106T205236Z-v0-constrained-qwen3-5-4b-q4-K-M-mini10-f918c1/toposort/trace.jsonl). It still had 6 incorrect submissions and 4 loop/step exits. Valid action syntax was not enough for correct programs.

**Targeted feedback recovered some actions.** The [repair run](runs/20261106T205929Z-v0-repair-qwen3-5-4b-q4-K-M-mini10-3f92b6/tasks.jsonl) recorded 27 parse errors and 6 format-budget exits. [intervals](runs/20261106T205929Z-v0-repair-qwen3-5-4b-q4-K-M-mini10-3f92b6/intervals/trace.jsonl) recovered from malformed calls and passed. [merge-config](runs/20261106T205929Z-v0-repair-qwen3-5-4b-q4-K-M-mini10-3f92b6/merge-config/trace.jsonl) shows the corrective instruction changing on repeated invalid replies without achieving a pass. This is a whole-run comparison, not proof that one individual message caused the pass.

**Alignment made a concrete edit safer.** The [JSONL CLI trace](runs/20261106T210256Z-v0-aligned-qwen3-5-4b-q4-K-M-mini10-ecef50/jsonl-cli/trace.jsonl) records a Python syntax rejection for rebinding a comprehension iteration variable, before file mutation. The same run also completed raw-code patch dispatches. It still ended 8 tasks on format budgets. Mechanical edit safety and task correctness are different outcomes.

**The requirement workflow remained mostly unreachable in isolation.** All 10 tasks ultimately ended on format budgets. Its 1 finish-gate attempt was blocked by a missing requirements artifact in [sql-revenue](runs/20261106T210659Z-v0-requirements-qwen3-5-4b-q4-K-M-mini10-8eddce/sql-revenue/trace.jsonl); 0 gates passed. This does not establish that executable self-tests are ineffective: the agent did not successfully reach that workflow.

**Version tracking removed a premature stop, but did not solve the task.** In [config-parser](runs/20261106T211034Z-v0-versions-qwen3-5-4b-q4-K-M-mini10-0e4fae/config-parser/trace.jsonl), rereads after edits continued through the fixed step budget rather than stopping at the original identical-read guard. The hidden verdict was still a failure. More allowed work is not automatically useful work. No hidden verifier content was inspected to diagnose or change the implementation.

**The declared combinations scored 3/10, 2/10 and 4/10.** The strongest observed configuration was [combo-constrained-aligned-versions-requirements-repair](runs/20261106T214547Z-combo-constrained-aligned-versions-requirements-repair-qwen3-5-4b-q4-K-M-mini10-f597e7/run.json), at 40%, 1030.19 seconds, 189,478 input tokens and 14,227 output tokens. It improved on the original v0's observed result but did not beat the baseline's five passes. This is a development-suite result from the declared sequence, not a held-out or statistical win.

**Passing self-tests did not establish correctness.** In [merge-config with requirement checks](runs/20261106T212825Z-combo-constrained-aligned-versions-requirements-qwen3-5-4b-q4-K-M-mini10-d054d7/merge-config/trace.jsonl), an initial gate was blocked by the missing requirements file. A later gate passed, but the independent verdict was failure. That run recorded 1 passed and 6 blocked gates; missing artifacts and assertion failures must not be conflated. It also reached loop/step exits on 9 tasks, showing the workflow's cost under the fixed budget.

**The final repair switch did not explain the score difference.** The final configuration emitted 0 repair-feedback events because it had 0 parse errors. It scored differently from the preceding configuration even though the added branch was never used. The [replay audit](research/phase2-replay-check.json) found identical first requests/responses on csv-totals, followed by changed tool observations (wall time and output). These single attempts cannot identify a causal repair benefit. No extra attempts were sampled to obtain a desired score.
selection: All five single changes were completed first. The declared combination sequence starts with constrained actions, alignment and file versions, then adds requirement checks, then targeted repair. Each later candidate adds one feature. The final choice uses pass count, then parse-error count, actual total tokens and task wall time; every candidate is reported. See [the combination plan](research/phase2-combination-plan.json). The observed selection under that rule is `combo-constrained-aligned-versions-requirements-repair`. The desired pass-rate win over the reference was not achieved.
post_findings: Raw code views and precommit syntax checking addressed a concrete edit problem, and the file-version guard stopped treating every reread after an edit as the same stalled action. These mechanical fixes did not guarantee correct programs.

Adding the requirement workflow changed the observed score from 3/10 to 2/10 and consumed more tokens. A self-test gate passed while the independent grader failed the same submission: matching task quotes and successful assertions did not prove adequate coverage.

The final configuration reached 4/10, but its added repair branch never ran. Tool timings and filesystem observations changed subsequent prompts despite a fixed seed. We cannot credit that score difference to repair, and the baseline's five passes were not exceeded.
